thread.title: Apple’s China problem just got worse after CEO Tim Cook waited to sound the alarm

author: Nigam Arora
title: Apple’s China problem just got worse after CEO Tim Cook waited to sound the alarm
text:
Apple CEO Tim Cook was the last person to know that Chinese consumers weren’t buying iPhones in ever-increasing numbers. That is, if you believe Apple’s public pronouncements and Wall Street analysts.
Cook said in a letter to investors Wednesday: “[W]e did not foresee the magnitude of the economic deceleration, particularly in Greater China.”
On the other hand, if you’re an astute investor, you already knew that Apple AAPL, -9.31% had an iPhone problem in China. (A problem for Apple is also brewing in India.) You don’t even need to be an astute investor. All you had to do was watch the price action in Apple’s stock. Price action is one of the most important tools to make money, and this is the reason that I teach it as a technique in my seminars.
Read: Apple’s biggest stock-price drops of the iPhone era: Where does today’s drop rank?
When Apple stock was trading in the $220 to $230 range, The Arora Report’s “buy now” rating on the stock was a “no” and the buy zone was suspended on concerns about China. Apple’s stock also did not rate favorably on the so-called Risk Reward Matrix. The key question now for investors is: “How low can Apple’s stock go?” Let’s explore with the help of two charts.
Charts Please click here for the Risk Reward Matrix.
Please click here for an annotated candlestick chart of Apple’s stock. Please note the following:
• The Risk Reward Matrix is very popular among investors because it gives investors an easy to understand visualization for picking stocks and to make buy, sell or hold decisions.
• The Risk Reward Matrix shows Apple compared with Google GOOG, -2.53% GOOGL, -2.57% Facebook FB, -2.50% Amazon AMZN, -1.92% and Netflix NFLX, +1.78%
• The comparison is also shown for semiconductor stocks Intel INTC, -4.50% NXP Semiconductors NXPI, -2.73% Qualcomm QCOM, -2.48% and Applied Materials AMAT, -4.64%
• To give investors a better understanding of how the Risk Reward Matrix works, also shown are non-technology stocks Walmart WMT, -0.07% Bank of America BAC, -0.94% J.P. Morgan JPM, -0.79% and T-Mobile TMUS, +0.41%
• The candlestick chart is a monthly chart of Apple.
• The chart shows two support zones for Apple.
• The higher support zone shown on the chart has a 55% probability of holding. If the name of the stock was hidden from the chart, no fundamental and macro factors were considered and a call was to be made simply based on the technicals, the probability of the stock holding the top support zone shown on the chart would have been about 10%. In the case of Apple, the probability of the top zone shown on the chart holding is so much higher because of huge buybacks by the company, a large cash position, a growing services business and the prospect of Trump striking a deal with China.
• If the higher support zone breaks, Apple is likely to fall to the lower support zone shown on the chart.
• The chart shows that The Arora Report “buy now” rating on Apple was a “no” and the Arora buy zone on Apple was suspended at a time when everybody was bullish on Apple and Apple’s stock was rocketing. Investors who followed along saved themselves a lot of pain.
• The chart shows the divergence between RSI (relative strength index) and the price of Apple stock. This was a telltale sign of the danger in this stock before it started falling.
• The chart shows that the stock is not yet oversold.
• The chart also shows the oversold threshold.
• Once a major stock like Apple gets oversold, the probability of a strong rally goes up significantly.
• Apple stock has very heavy weightings in indexes. Therefore, it has a significant impact on the Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, -2.44% S&P 500 ETF SPY, -1.97% and Nasdaq 100 ETF QQQ, -2.83%

Tim Cook was the last to know? Was Tim Cook really the last person to know? Did major Wall Street analysts really not know what was going on in China with the iPhone? Is the trust broken now? If so, what impact would that have on Apple’s stock? (Analysts at Macquarie said: “The bottom line is that we are late (obviously), but we can no longer recommend AAPL.”) The answers would be obvious to astute investors who have carefully studied how the system works.
Apple advantage One advantage that Apple has is that it is an inexpensive stock. Investors who are overly concentrated in high-flying, expensive stocks such as ANGI Homeservices ANGI, -3.23% Etsy ETSY, -0.21% Twilio TWLO, -5.01% and Workday WDAY, -4.24% should carefully review their position sizes. Under some scenarios, high-flying tech stocks can fall by 50%. Please see my call on this CNBC segment . For proof, take a look at AMD AMD, -9.32% and Nvidia NVDA, -5.91% Please see “ The poster child of bull-market excess just dimmed the prospects of the broader stock market ” and “ There’s a ‘shooting star’ in the way of AMD’s stock rising higher .” The Arora Report gave a partial sell signal on AMD at $33.60 and raised the stops.
The biggest danger The biggest danger to Apple stock is not its fundamentals or the macro picture, but the fact that the stock is over-owned. This will be the subject of a future post. If you have been a longtime reader, you have probably already learned and implemented this important concept.
What to do now Apple is at an inflection point. A lot can go right, but a lot can go wrong too. Investors may want to learn several techniques that can be invaluable to them. One technique is to hold on to a core position and then surround it with trade-around positions. For example, The Arora Report is holding a core position in Apple stock from $18.73 but has made significant profits in addition to the core position by using those techniques.
